newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on yen's steep fall vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on yen's steep fall vs dlr.

text.p: The key December Euroyen futures contract ended weaker on Wednesday because of the yen's steep fall against the dollar, traders said.
By 0720 GMT, the yen had fallen to a low of around 122.75 to the dollar, setting a new 47-month low. It had ended at 120.95/05 to the dollar in New York on Tuesday.
The yen's fall is, in theory, inflationary as it pushes up import prices, putting upward pressure on interest rates.
Despite the fall in Euroyen prices today, some said that the magnitude of the losses was small.

"The Euroyen could have fallen much further on the yen's tumble, but, many think that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will not be able to tighten credit to defend the yen in view of the nation's bad loan problem," said a European bank trader.
The key December fell as low as 99.17 during the day, before ending at 99.18.
Support for the December now lies at 99.15 which is also a 20-day moving average, traders said.
